judgment_calls: task-reducer.ts (src/store) is NOT edited by this story -- kept exactly as-is with its own inline three-level comparator. bound-4.structural.test.ts's repo-wide duplicate-comparator scan explicitly allowlists it (ALLOWLISTED_LEGACY_FILES) with an expiry comment pointing at S9 (task-store-projection-cutover) / S12 (legacy-listener-removal). Chosen over delegating task-reducer.ts to taskWinsOver in this story despite architecture.md Implementation Constraint 10 naming task-reducer.ts:18-32 as one of two required delegation sites, because (1) stories.json's S3 scope.includes lists exactly six files, none of which is task-reducer.ts, (2) the story text explicitly instructs 'do NOT change task-reducer.ts's behavior in this story', and (3) task-reducer.ts carries a 147/147 mutation-kill record on a file-scoped Stryker config (stryker.task-reducer.conf.json) that delegation would silently relocate/stale without an in-scope mutation re-run. Implementation Constraint 10 is read as satisfied incrementally, matching this epic's stated strangler-fig pattern elsewhere (device-sync.ts / task-store.tsx: 'Shrinking: internals migrate story-by-story'). Documented in architecture.json judgment call 'task-reducer-allowlist-not-delegate' and verification.json VQ-S3-010 (post-impl, confidence 1.0).

TaskProjection is a bare `ReadonlyMap<string, Task>` (mirroring task-reducer.ts's TaskState = Map<string, Task> exactly), with NO explicit applied-event-id bookkeeping (no Set<string> of seen ids). AC-INV-2's projector-side duplicate-id idempotency is satisfied purely because taskWinsOver's strict inequalities make every TaskEvent variant naturally idempotent under re-application (task.created is first-write-wins via a has() guard; the four tie-break variants all require a STRICT win over the current existing state, and a byte-identical duplicate re-delivery can never strictly beat the state it already produced). Proven directly by the >=100-run AC-INV-2 property test (splicing a reference-identical duplicate adjacent to the original and asserting buildProjection is unchanged), not asserted only by argument. Documented in architecture.json judgment calls 'projection-shape-readonly-map' and 'no-explicit-dedup-bookkeeping', and verification.json VQ-S3-013 (post-impl, confidence 1.0).

bound-4.structural.test.ts's CANONICAL_FILES allowlist (the set exempted from the AC-BOUND-4 duplicate-comparator scan as 'the one true implementation') contains two exact paths: src/domain/task-crdt.ts (the real implementation) and src/domain/task-crdt.test.ts (whose legacyInlineComparator helper deliberately reconstructs the exact legacy expression as a parity-proof fixture, never called by production code). empirical_verification.ac_bound_4_flip_check: Performed manually per the story's quality-gate instruction: temporarily re-pasted the exact deleted inline comparator body back into device-sync.ts's `wins` computation (undoing the taskWinsOver delegation), ran `npx vitest run src/domain/bound-4.structural.test.ts`, and confirmed 3 of 13 tests went RED (the two import-assertion-adjacent checks and the repo-wide violations=[] assertion, which reported `violations: ["src/marmot/device-sync.ts"]`). Reverted device-sync.ts back to the taskWinsOver call and re-ran the same test file, confirming all 13 tests green again. Re-ran the full suite (696/696) and `npx tsc --noEmit` (exit 0) after the revert to confirm no residual damage from the manual edit-revert cycle.

retrospective.harder_than_needed: Reconciling the exact tests_added breakdown against the full-suite baseline/final delta required discovering, empirically, that two PRE-EXISTING structural test suites (domain-boundary.structural.test.ts and engine-boundary.structural.test.ts, both authored in S1/S2) walk the filesystem and emit one test-case per file discovered under src/domain/ -- so simply summing the 'obvious' new test files' own standalone counts (19+5+13=37) undercounted the true delta (56) by 19, all silently absorbed into two files this story never touched. Diagnosed by temporarily relocating the new src/domain/ files out of the tree and re-running the two suites standalone to get true before/after per-file deltas (48->60 and 105->110). Not a correctness problem -- the self-scaling scanners are working exactly as designed by S1/S2 -- but it is a real reporting trap for any story that adds files under a directory a self-scanning structural test already covers, worth flagging so a future story doesn't just report its own new test files' counts as the total tests_added delta without checking for this effect.
